references.text: Pharaoh confesses his sin with similar words: 'I have sinned'. Both cases show a confession under pressure from God's intervention.
Achan uses the same expression 'I have sinned' when confronted with his disobedience, a pattern of confession in the Old Testament.
Saul confesses 'I have sinned' after being confronted by Samuel. A similar situation where a person acknowledges sin following divine rebuke.
Saul says again to David, 'I have sinned', and admits that he acted in ignorance and folly, parallel to Balaam's acknowledgment of ignorance.
David confesses 'I have sinned against the Lord' to the prophet Nathan. Another example of confession following divine confrontation.
David acknowledges his sin with the words 'I have sinned greatly', a similar formula of confession used by Balaam.
The context in which the angel of the Lord reveals himself to Balaam and opens his eyes, leading to the confession in verse 34.
Judas says, 'I have sinned by betraying innocent blood'. A similar formula of confession, but without genuine repentance.
The prodigal son plans to say, 'I have sinned against heaven and against you'. An example of confession in Jesus' parable.
